One page, no build, nothing from elsewhere

The rules of a factory page

It runs from file://, on GitHub Pages and as a claude.ai artifact, whose content security policy blocks every request to elsewhere.

Accessibility is part of the work

The canvas is an image with a written description, the figures are output elements, and the table of machines is the keyboard route to every action.

Physical correctness first

Nothing passes through anything else. An impossible move is flagged and counted, never hidden.

Every thing is a box

  function B(x0, y0, z0, x1, y1, z1, c, extra) {
    const b = { x0, y0, z0, x1, y1, z1, c, tag: TAG };
    if (extra) {
      Object.assign(b, extra);
      // the render cache recognises a box by position, size, colour, a, ns and stripes; a box
      // carrying anything else that might affect drawing is never cached, just drawn live
      for (const k in extra) if (k !== 'a' && k !== 'ns' && k !== 'stripes') { b.nocache = true; break; }
    }
    boxes.push(b);
    return b;
  }

One arm over the shared floor

  // The floor both depalletizers reach over: the belt where the layers go down and the rack beside
  // it. Only one works over it at a time: a move that takes the head over it waits until the other
  // has gone (sharedBy). With heads a layer wide, their paths to the belt and the rack cross, and
  // waiting step by step for each other there left both stuck. (The lowest slot on the leg, which
  // they both pick from too, isn't in it: what they go for there is reserved, and one holding a
  // layer over it while the belt is full would keep the other from the rack.)
  const SHARED = [[2.4, 1.6, 4.9, 5.0]];
  const inShared = p => SHARED.some(([x0, y0, x1, y1]) => p[0] > x0 && p[0] < x1 && p[1] > y0 && p[1] < y1);
  const overShared = (arm, a, b) => { for (let k = 0; k <= 1.0001; k += 0.1) if (inShared(turnLerp(arm, a, b, k))) return true; return false; };

When each waits for the other

    const stuck = () => {

        sim.armYield = { arm: who, t: sim.t }; sim.armDeadlocks = (sim.armDeadlocks || 0) + 1;
      }
      return sim.armYield.arm === arm;
    };

A rule of the line

If each is waiting for the other, one moves out of the way, round to its rest, and carries on from there.

  const RES = new Map();                       // mover -> { list, x0, y0, x1, y1, t0, t1, l }
  const FOREVER = 1e9;
  const RES_PAD = 0.15;                        // s either side of every window: setting off a frame late, rounding
  const PIECE = 0.25, LEG_SLACK = 0.04, LATE = 0.3, HORIZON = 300, MAX_LEGS = 10;
  const levelsAt = z => z < 0.5 ? 1 : z > 1.3 ? 2 : 3;

The reservation table

  function resHit(m, b, m2) {
    let hit = null;
    for (const [who, r] of RES) {
      if (who === m || who === m2 || !(r.l & b.l) || r.t1 <= b.t0 || b.t1 <= r.t0 || !boxesMeet(r, b)) continue;
      for (const q of r.list) if ((q.l & b.l) && q.t0 < b.t1 && b.t0 < q.t1 && boxesMeet(q, b) && (!hit || q.t1 > hit.t1)) hit = { who, t0: q.t0, t1: q.t1, q };
    }
    return hit;
  }

When a plan runs into someone

  1. Someone idle steps aside, waits a moment, and goes back
  2. Someone busy: after 3 s, go round them, or another way
  3. Failing both, go round firmly: the idle step aside on arrival
  4. Failing all, walk as far as you can and try again
  5. Lifts nose to nose: the one with less far to go backs off

A monitor, not a constraint

Flag, never prevent

Impossible moves are logged and counted. A guard that silently stopped them would hide the bug.
  • Lifts against each other and against people on foot
  • People and robots against each other, on the same level
  • Feet against the treads of the stairs
  • A jam check too: nobody with work still for over a minute

Two samples, one window

  function oeeFigures(from, to) {
    const planned = to.t - from.t;
    if (planned < 30) return null;
    const run = Math.max(0, planned - (to.stop - from.stop));
    const total = to.total - from.total, scrap = to.scrap - from.scrap;
    const A = run / planned;
    const P = run > 0 ? IDEAL_CYCLE * total / run : 0;
    const Q = total > 0 ? Math.max(0, total - scrap) / total : 1;
    return { A, P, Q, oee: A * P * Q };
  }

  let faultScale = 8;
  function setFaultScale(v) {
    const k = v / faultScale; faultScale = v;
    for (const m of [...Object.values(machines), ...robots, ...forklifts]) if (!m.down && m.nextFail !== undefined && m.nextFail > sim.t) m.nextFail = sim.t + (m.nextFail - sim.t) * k;
  }
  $('faultRate').addEventListener('change', e => setFaultScale(parseFloat(e.target.value)));

Why not the simulation in Elixir

Every sub-step needs one consistent view of the whole floor. One process per actor turns that into a coordination problem.

On screen, a box is a hexagon, and a hexagon is the intersection of three slabs in u, v and w. Two boxes overlap on screen exactly when their three intervals overlap.

When no order is possible

rellen.github.io/iso-factories · line-4/index.html
7 / 28
Three boxes can each be behind the next along a different axis. The sort finds the cycle and releases the member whose broken orders share the least screen area. It never releases a box that only waits behind a cycle.

When each waits for the other

    const stuck = () => {
      if (!(o.waiting && arm.waiting)) return false;
      if (!sim.armYield) {
        const who = going(arm) !== going(o) ? (going(arm) ? o : arm) : arm.zoneWait !== !!o.zoneWait ? (arm.zoneWait ? arm : o) : Math.random() < 0.5 ? arm : o;
        sim.armYield = { arm: who, t: sim.t }; sim.armDeadlocks = (sim.armDeadlocks || 0) + 1;
      }
      return sim.armYield.arm === arm;
    };

If each is waiting for the other, one moves out of the way, round to its rest, and carries on from there.

Book the floor before you move

rellen.github.io/iso-factories · line-4/index.html
12 / 28
Two lifts share a lane one lift wide. People and robots cross it and walk along it. Everyone books floor in space and time before moving, so nobody moves through anybody else. Here A has booked its walk; B asks for a window to cross, finds A, and crosses after A has passed.

The reservation table

  function resHit(m, b, m2) {
    let hit = null;
    for (const [who, r] of RES) {
      if (who === m || who === m2 || !(r.l & b.l) || r.t1 <= b.t0 || b.t1 <= r.t0 || !boxesMeet(r, b)) continue;
      for (const q of r.list) if ((q.l & b.l) && q.t0 < b.t1 && b.t0 < q.t1 && boxesMeet(q, b) && (!hit || q.t1 > hit.t1)) hit = { who, t0: q.t0, t1: q.t1, q };
    }
    return hit;
  }

When a plan runs into someone

  1. Someone idle steps aside, waits a moment, and goes back
  2. Someone busy: after 3 s, go round them, or another way
  3. Failing both, go round firmly: the idle step aside on arrival
  4. Failing all, walk as far as you can and try again
  5. Lifts nose to nose: the one with less far to go backs off
rellen.github.io/iso-factories · line-4/index.html
15 / 28
The order matters, and each step came from a deadlock found in a long run. The table costs about 3% of the throughput: people now queue for each other where they used to walk through.

A monitor, not a constraint

Flag, never prevent

Impossible moves are logged and counted. A guard that silently stopped them would hide the bug.
  • Lifts against each other and against people on foot
  • People and robots against each other, on the same level
  • Feet against the treads of the stairs
  • A jam check too: nobody with work still for over a minute
rellen.github.io/iso-factories · line-4/index.html
18 / 28
The physics check never stops a move. It logs it in sim.viol.list and counts it in the status panel. A change to layout or routing must leave the count at zero over a long run: sixteen seeds, eight hours each.

OEE = Availability × Performance × Quality

rellen.github.io/iso-factories · line-4/index.html
19 / 28
OEE is counted at the painter. A stop of 60 seconds or more costs availability, slow running and short stops cost performance, and anything not good first time costs quality. The rated cycle is 0.45 s, 8,000 an hour, ahead of the line at every setting.
Northside Works · Line 4

Two samples, one window

  function oeeFigures(from, to) {
    const planned = to.t - from.t;
    if (planned < 30) return null;
    const run = Math.max(0, planned - (to.stop - from.stop));
    const total = to.total - from.total, scrap = to.scrap - from.scrap;
    const A = run / planned;
    const P = run > 0 ? IDEAL_CYCLE * total / run : 0;
    const Q = total > 0 ? Math.max(0, total - scrap) / total : 1;
    return { A, P, Q, oee: A * P * Q };
  }

Settings that start at world class

  let faultScale = 8;
  function setFaultScale(v) {
    const k = v / faultScale; faultScale = v;
    for (const m of [...Object.values(machines), ...robots, ...forklifts]) if (!m.down && m.nextFail !== undefined && m.nextFail > sim.t) m.nextFail = sim.t + (m.nextFail - sim.t) * k;
  }
  $('faultRate').addEventListener('change', e => setFaultScale(parseFloat(e.target.value)));

Where each part goes

PartGoes toBecause
Simulationa Rust cratetyped, fast, deterministic, builds for both hosts
DrawingTypeScriptit is already JavaScript
Serving, viewers, historyElixir and Phoenixsupervision, fan-out, persistence

Why not the simulation in Elixir

Every sub-step needs one consistent view of the whole floor. One process per actor turns that into a coordination problem.
rellen.github.io/iso-factories · line-4/index.html
25 / 28
Planning only: nothing is ported. First separate the simulation from the drawing in the page itself, with the jam harness running throughout. Then one Rust crate with two hosts: WebAssembly in the browser, and a Rustler NIF on the server.

    One page, no build, nothing from elsewhere

    The rules of a factory page

    It runs from file://, on GitHub Pages and as a claude.ai artifact, whose content security policy blocks every request to elsewhere.

    Accessibility is part of the work

    The canvas is an image with a written description, the figures are output elements, and the table of machines is the keyboard route to every action.

    Physical correctness first

    Nothing passes through anything else. An impossible move is flagged and counted, never hidden.

    Every thing is a box

      function B(x0, y0, z0, x1, y1, z1, c, extra) {
    const b = { x0, y0, z0, x1, y1, z1, c, tag: TAG };
    if (extra) {
      Object.assign(b, extra);
      // the render cache recognises a box by position, size, colour, a, ns and stripes; a box
      // carrying anything else that might affect drawing is never cached, just drawn live
      for (const k in extra) if (k !== 'a' && k !== 'ns' && k !== 'stripes') { b.nocache = true; break; }
    }
    boxes.push(b);
    return b;
  }

    Two arms, one belt

    • Each takes a whole layer and sets it on belt A1, a row in each lane
    • Neither moves into the other: a 3D check of every part, 5 cm to spare
    • Only one works over the belt and the rack at a time
    • Each picks the most downstream pallet it can reach first

    One arm over the shared floor

      // The floor both depalletizers reach over: the belt where the layers go down and the rack beside
  // it. Only one works over it at a time: a move that takes the head over it waits until the other
  // has gone (sharedBy). With heads a layer wide, their paths to the belt and the rack cross, and
  // waiting step by step for each other there left both stuck. (The lowest slot on the leg, which
  // they both pick from too, isn't in it: what they go for there is reserved, and one holding a
  // layer over it while the belt is full would keep the other from the rack.)
  const SHARED = [[2.4, 1.6, 4.9, 5.0]];
  const inShared = p => SHARED.some(([x0, y0, x1, y1]) => p[0] > x0 && p[0] < x1 && p[1] > y0 && p[1] < y1);
  const overShared = (arm, a, b) => { for (let k = 0; k <= 1.0001; k += 0.1) if (inShared(turnLerp(arm, a, b, k))) return true; return false; };

    When each waits for the other

        const stuck = () => {
      if (!(o.waiting && arm.waiting)) return false;
      if (!sim.armYield) {
        const who = going(arm) !== going(o) ? (going(arm) ? o : arm) : arm.zoneWait !== !!o.zoneWait ? (arm.zoneWait ? arm : o) : Math.random() < 0.5 ? arm : o;
        sim.armYield = { arm: who, t: sim.t }; sim.armDeadlocks = (sim.armDeadlocks || 0) + 1;
      }
      return sim.armYield.arm === arm;
    };

    A rule of the line

    If each is waiting for the other, one moves out of the way, round to its rest, and carries on from there.

    The reservation table

      function resHit(m, b, m2) {
    let hit = null;
    for (const [who, r] of RES) {
      if (who === m || who === m2 || !(r.l & b.l) || r.t1 <= b.t0 || b.t1 <= r.t0 || !boxesMeet(r, b)) continue;
      for (const q of r.list) if ((q.l & b.l) && q.t0 < b.t1 && b.t0 < q.t1 && boxesMeet(q, b) && (!hit || q.t1 > hit.t1)) hit = { who, t0: q.t0, t1: q.t1, q };
    }
    return hit;
  }

    When a plan runs into someone

    1. Someone idle steps aside, waits a moment, and goes back
    2. Someone busy: after 3 s, go round them, or another way
    3. Failing both, go round firmly: the idle step aside on arrival
    4. Failing all, walk as far as you can and try again
    5. Lifts nose to nose: the one with less far to go backs off

    A monitor, not a constraint

    Flag, never prevent

    Impossible moves are logged and counted. A guard that silently stopped them would hide the bug.
    • Lifts against each other and against people on foot
    • People and robots against each other, on the same level
    • Feet against the treads of the stairs
    • A jam check too: nobody with work still for over a minute

    Two samples, one window

      function oeeFigures(from, to) {
    const planned = to.t - from.t;
    if (planned < 30) return null;
    const run = Math.max(0, planned - (to.stop - from.stop));
    const total = to.total - from.total, scrap = to.scrap - from.scrap;
    const A = run / planned;
    const P = run > 0 ? IDEAL_CYCLE * total / run : 0;
    const Q = total > 0 ? Math.max(0, total - scrap) / total : 1;
    return { A, P, Q, oee: A * P * Q };
  }

      let faultScale = 8;
  function setFaultScale(v) {
    const k = v / faultScale; faultScale = v;
    for (const m of [...Object.values(machines), ...robots, ...forklifts]) if (!m.down && m.nextFail !== undefined && m.nextFail > sim.t) m.nextFail = sim.t + (m.nextFail - sim.t) * k;
  }
  $('faultRate').addEventListener('change', e => setFaultScale(parseFloat(e.target.value)));
